# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual, but I cannot speak - only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. Blind needs to know which wire to cut, but Blind can't see gestures. I need to relay information to Deaf first, who then presumably will need to communicate to Blind somehow - but Deaf can't speak either (deaf can't hear, but can they speak? Let me check: Deaf "cannot hear anything, or touch the bomb" - speaking isn't excluded, so Deaf CAN speak).

So the chain is: Mute (me) → gesture → Deaf sees gesture + sees bomb light color → Deaf speaks → Blind hears and cuts wire.

I need a gesture encoding for the three light→wire mappings. Let me establish a simple code: I'll assign one distinct gesture per light color, paired with the correct cut color, so Deaf can learn the mapping and combine it with what they see.

Since this is turn 1 and I go first, Deaf hasn't seen the bomb's actual light yet in terms of reporting back, but I don't know the current light state anyway - only Deaf sees the bomb. So I should just teach the general mapping now, so Deaf can apply it once they see the light.

I'll use three gesture pairs to encode: green→red, red→yellow, yellow→green.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "☝"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows 0. Light is green. Three wires: wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 red.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf saw the bomb: light is green, and there's a wire numbering (wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 red). Per the manual, green light means cut the red wire, which is wire 3.

Deaf gestured back "👍" to me - likely acknowledging receipt of my earlier gesture code (👍=green pairs with ✊=red), confirming they understood my mapping attempt. But I have no way to know if they correctly parsed all three pairs since gestures are just symbol sequences without inherent meaning until established - my previous turn tried to define green→red, red→yellow, yellow→green using 👍/✊, 👌/✌, 🖐/☝ pairs.

Since Deaf already reported the light color and wire arrangement via speech (which I cannot hear... wait, I'm Mute, can I hear? Let me check: Mute "cannot speak" - hearing isn't excluded. So I CAN hear Deaf's speech.

So I heard: light is green, wires are 1=yellow, 2=green, 3=red. Manual says green light → cut red wire. Red wire is wire 3.

I need to confirm this specific instruction to Deaf via gesture so Deaf can relay to Blind by speech. I'll gesture confirmation using my established code for green→red (👍 then ✊), and also need to convey "wire 3" - I should establish a number gesture too.

Let me use ☝✌🤟 as a simple counting system for wire 1,2,3 and combine with the red designation.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✊", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]

Deaf sent back a single gesture "☝" - this could be an acknowledgment or a question, but I can't be certain what it means since we haven't fully established a shared code yet. Deaf can see the bomb and already reported the light is green with wires: 1=yellow, 2=green, 3=red. I confirmed via gesture 👍✊🤟 meaning "green→red→wire3" using my established pairs (👍=green, ✊=red, 🤟=three).

Since Deaf can speak and hear is not restricted for them, but wait - Deaf "cannot hear anything" - so Deaf cannot hear Blind or me speaking. Deaf can only receive gestures from me, and speaks to whoever can hear (Blind and Mute both can hear, since only Deaf is deaf).

So Deaf needs to speak the instruction to Blind directly: "cut the red wire" or "cut wire 3". Deaf has all the info needed already from their own sight plus my gesture confirming the manual rule. Deaf should just speak to Blind now.

My job here is likely done unless Deaf needs more clarification. The "☝" might be Deaf trying to confirm wire number 1, or just acknowledging. Since I can't verify, I'll wait and see if Deaf speaks to Blind, but I should also make sure Deaf actually got the right pairing - let me resend clearly once more or wait.

Since gestures only carry meaning through prior mutual establishment, and I only have this one exchange, I'll assume Deaf understood "green→red, red→yellow, yellow→green" from turn 1, and turn 2 I confirmed "green→red, wire 3". The ☝ might mean "wire 1?" - a doubt. Let me clarify wire 3 more firmly.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I see your gestures but do not have a fixed code yet. Let's use finger counts for wire numbers: one finger means wire 1, two fingers means wire 2, three fingers means wire 3. Use thumbs up after the number to confirm cut that wire, thumbs down to say do not cut. Repeat your instruction now using this code.

Deaf has proposed a clear code: finger-count gesture for wire number (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3), followed by 👍 to confirm "cut this wire" or 👎 for "do not cut".

The bomb: light green, wire 1=yellow, wire 2=green, wire 3=red. Manual: green light → cut red wire. Red is wire 3.

So I need to tell Deaf: wire 3, cut it. That's 🤟 then 👍.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Understood: wire 3, cut confirmed. Relaying to Blind now.

Deaf has confirmed understanding and is relaying "wire 3, cut" to Blind now. My job for this round is done - the correct instruction (cut wire 3, which is red, matching the green light per the manual) has been successfully communicated through the gesture code we established.

I'll wait to see if any further clarification is needed, or if a new round/bomb state arises.

```
wait()
```
